title: Algebraic points on a circle plus at most three arbitrary points are Euclidean Ramsey
summary: Theorem B(b): finitely many distinct points on a circle in the Euclidean plane (centre and radius arbitrary reals), all of whose coordinates are algebraic over Q except for the points with indices in a set T of at most three, form a Euclidean Ramsey configuration. Ramsey is OpenAI's definition from result 172 (for every r >= 2 there is D such that every r-colouring of R^D contains a monochromatic congruent copy).
